sentences.text: Jiangxisaurus was an extinct theropod dinosaur belonging to the oviraptorid family, discovered in southern China.
This animal looked similar to Heyuannia but had more strongly curved front claws and a thinner, more fragile lower jaw.
The holotype skull, which is the specimen the species is based on, measures 150mm in length and represents a sub-adult individual.
Its mandible was toothless and had a height-to-length ratio of approximately 20%.
The radius of the arm is 96mm long, which is 30% shorter than its 136mm humerus.
The hand was tridactyl, featuring a robust first finger, an elongated second finger, and a slender third finger.
Researchers identified unique features including a weakly down-turned jaw symphysis, a concave suprangular bone, and a very elongated mandible.
It was likely an omnivore, sharing this diet with its close relatives Nankangia and Ganzhousaurus.
The genus Jiangxisaurus was described and named by Wei Xuefang, Pu Hanyong, Xu Li, Liu Di, and Lü Junchang in 2013.
The genus name honors Jiangxi Province, while the species name ganzhouensis refers to Ganzhou, the specific site of discovery.
The only known specimen was found at the Nankang locality in Ganzhou City, Jiangxi Province, China.
Jiangxisaurus is classified within the dinosaur family Oviraptoridae.
Jiangxisaurus lived during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 72 to 66 million years ago.
Jiangxisaurus ganzhouensis is the only known species of this extinct genus, living in Asia during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 72 to 66 million years ago.
The specimen was collected from red sandstone sediments deposited during the Maastrichtian stage of the Cretaceous, approximately 72 to 66 million years ago.
The time range for Jiangxisaurus is the Maastrichtian, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
